articles.title: Meal Delivery Service CookUnity to Open Flagship Storefront at NoMad Hotel
articles.narrative: CookUnity, a subscription-based meal delivery service, has secured 4,721 square feet of ground-floor retail space at the Virgin Hotel New York City in Manhattan's NoMad neighborhood. This transaction marks the company's first flagship storefront in New York City, which will offer dining, retail, and community gathering spaces, signifying a strategic expansion beyond its delivery-only model. The new location is anticipated to open in the first half of 2027.

data_points.notable_features: Located in a 38-story hotel tower with over 400 rooms, a rooftop pool, and a restaurant.

articles.market_intelligence: The average asking rent for retail space in the Herald Square neighborhood, near NoMad, was $394 per square foot during the second quarter of 2026.

articles.title: It’s Finally Showtime Again at Hollywood’s Cinerama Dome
articles.narrative: Sony Pictures Entertainment and its subsidiary, Alamo Drafthouse Cinema, have signed a long-term lease to restore and reopen the iconic Cinerama Dome and the adjacent 14-screen former ArcLight Cinemas complex in Hollywood, six years after their closure. The Cinerama Dome, a Los Angeles Historic Cultural Monument, will preserve its unique curved screen and large-format presentation, while the neighboring multiplex will reopen as an Alamo Drafthouse with dine-in service. This significant lease is seen as a strong vote of confidence in the future of theatrical entertainment and the demand for shared moviegoing experiences, marking an exciting new chapter for a beloved cultural landmark.

data_points.notable_features: Los Angeles Historic Cultural Monument with an 86-foot-wide curved screen, known for 70-millimeter film presentations. The adjacent multiplex will feature 4K laser projection and 70-millimeter cinematic capabilities.
data_points.project_notes: The Cinerama Dome is expected to reopen in early 2028, with renovations beginning in August 2026. The property closed in March 2020, and ArcLight announced in 2021 it would not reopen its theaters.

people.name: Tom Rothman
people.title: Chairman and CEO of Motion Picture Group

articles.title: Bascom Buys 183-Unit Orange County, Calif., Complex for $53M
articles.narrative: The Bascom Group has acquired Castlewood Park Apartments, a 183-unit multifamily complex in Buena Park, CA, for $53.1 million. This acquisition expands Bascom's multifamily portfolio in the Western U.S., with plans to renovate apartment interiors, upgrade amenities, and enhance on-site management. The property represents a significant transaction in a supply-constrained Orange County submarket.

data_points.notable_features: Comprises 46 buildings, with two-, three-, and four-bedroom apartments averaging 1,028 square feet, adjacent to Buena Park High School.
data_points.project_notes: The property was renovated multiple times between 2010 and 2023. Bascom plans further interior renovations and amenity upgrades.

articles.market_intelligence: Buena Park is identified as one of the most supply-constrained submarkets in Orange County. This transaction is the largest multifamily sale in Buena Park and one of only eight multifamily sales over $50 million in north Orange County in the last 24 months.

articles.title: JP Morgan Finances Recap of Industrial Portfolio With $209M Loan
articles.narrative: A joint venture between Centerbridge Partners and Henderson Group secured a $208.5 million floating-rate loan from J.P. Morgan Chase to recapitalize a 40-asset industrial portfolio. The portfolio, spanning Pennsylvania and South Florida, encompasses 2.3 million square feet of last-mile warehouses, distribution sites, and shallow-bay facilities. The properties are 95 percent leased to a diverse tenant mix.

data_points.notable_features: Portfolio includes last-mile warehouses, distribution sites, and shallow-bay facilities with buildings ranging from 16,000 to 155,000 square feet.
data_points.project_notes: Five-year, floating-rate loan for recapitalization.

articles.title: CDK Lending Supplies $37M Loan for Newark Apartments Project
articles.narrative: RBH Group secured $36.7 million in pre-development financing from CDK Lending for a 420-unit mixed-use multifamily project in Newark, NJ. The loan retires previous debt from Goldman Sachs and will advance the long-planned development, which includes ground-floor retail. The project is situated on a 5.65-acre land assemblage in the Four Corners neighborhood, a site that has been under assembly since 2005.

data_points.notable_features: Located in Newark's Four Corners neighborhood near downtown, roughly half a mile from Newark Penn Station.
data_points.project_notes: The 5.65-acre site consists of 49 separate contiguous lots and has been under land assemblage since 2005.

articles.title: JLL Arranges Construction Debt, Joint Venture Equity for Dallas Mixed-Use Project
articles.narrative: JLL has arranged construction debt and joint venture equity for 8300 Douglas, a new mixed-use development in Dallas's Preston Center submarket. The project will feature a 12-story office building, a 17-story residential tower with 147 units, and significant retail space, along with a rooftop park. RAMROCK Real Estate is spearheading the development in collaboration with Lincoln Property Co. and Willow Bridge Property Co.

data_points.notable_features: Includes a 35,000-square-foot rooftop park and will house the regional headquarters of Fifth Third Bank.

articles.financing: Construction debt and joint venture equity

articles.title: Urban Logistics Realty to Develop Two Industrial Projects Totaling 341,000 SF in North Houston
articles.narrative: Urban Logistics Realty, in a joint venture with Principal Asset Management, is developing two industrial projects totaling 341,000 square feet in North Houston. The projects, Urban NXS Fallbrook and Urban NXS West, will be a cross-dock and front-load industrial building, respectively. Construction is expected to commence by late summer and conclude in the second quarter of 2027, with financing provided by First United Bank & Trust.

data_points.property_name: Urban NXS Fallbrook / Urban NXS West

articles.title: Realterm Buys 40-Acre Industrial Outdoor Storage Facility in Laredo, Texas
articles.narrative: Realterm, an investment manager specializing in transit-oriented properties, has acquired a 40-acre industrial outdoor storage (IOS) facility in Laredo, Texas. The property includes 25.3 acres of concrete paving, a check-in station, an office, and a wash bay. At the time of sale, a portion of the facility was leased to a transit firm.

data_points.notable_features: Features 25.3 concrete-paved acres, a 22,250-square-foot check-in station, a 6,800-square-foot office, and a 3,000-square-foot wash bay.
data_points.project_notes: A portion of the facility was leased to Heartland Express at the time of sale.

articles.title: Hoar Construction Breaks Ground on 32,000 SF Medical Office Building in East Austin
articles.narrative: Hoar Construction has broken ground on the Colony Park Health & Wellness Center, a four-story medical office building spanning 32,000 square feet in East Austin. The facility, owned by Central Health and designed by HKS Architects, will feature a pharmacy, lab, kitchen, patient care rooms, and a dental office across its upper floors, with utilities on the ground level. Completion is anticipated for summer 2027.

data_points.address: 1111 E Cesar Chavez St, Austin, TX

articles.title: Partnership Agrees to Acquire Providence Place Mall in Rhode Island for $133M
articles.narrative: A partnership comprising Pyramid Management Group, Paolino Properties, and DW Partners has agreed to acquire Providence Place Mall, a 1.4 million-square-foot lifestyle center in Providence, Rhode Island, for $133 million. The property had been under court-ordered receivership for several years due to a loan default by its previous owner. The new ownership intends to continue an ongoing repositioning program at the mall.

data_points.notable_features: Lifestyle center.
data_points.project_notes: Property was in court-ordered receivership following a loan default by the previous owner.

articles.title: Columbus office market nets fifth straight quarter of positive net absorption
articles.narrative: The Columbus, OH office market recorded its fifth consecutive quarter of positive net absorption in Q2 2026, totaling 68,171 square feet and bringing the year-to-date total to 179,294 square feet. This steady leasing activity has contributed to a gradual decline in the overall vacancy rate, which fell 30 basis points to 20.3%. The recovery is primarily driven by suburban submarkets, which accounted for the majority of positive absorption, while downtown Columbus continues to face challenges with negative absorption and higher vacancy rates. Limited new construction is also helping stabilize market fundamentals, with only 195,048 square feet currently under construction.
articles.market_intelligence: The Columbus office market's overall vacancy rate declined 30 basis points to 20.3% in Q2 2026. Suburban office submarkets accounted for 71,465 square feet of positive absorption, while downtown Columbus posted negative absorption of 3,294 square feet. No new office buildings were delivered in H1 2026, with only 195,048 square feet remaining under construction. Q2 2026 leasing volume was 620,323 square feet, 20% below the 16-year Q2 average. Average asking rents held steady at $23.13 per square foot, representing 4.1% year-to-date growth. Average office sale prices climbed to $104 per square foot, but excluding The Pointe at Polaris sale, the average was $57 per square foot.

articles.title: Game Changers: How Collaboration, Credibility, and Capital Are Rewriting Cleveland’s Real Estate Story
articles.narrative: Cleveland's commercial real estate market is undergoing a significant transformation, moving beyond isolated projects to a system-wide, collaborative approach that integrates development, infrastructure, talent, and innovation. This shift is supported by Ohio's top ranking for business and infrastructure, offering strategic advantages like market access and cost predictability. While office vacancy remains elevated, high-quality assets are outperforming, and industrial demand is healthy, particularly from advanced manufacturing and technology users. The region's focus on proactive business attraction, leveraging assets like NASA Glenn Research Center, and investments in quality-of-life amenities are key to unlocking sustained growth and competing nationally on factors beyond just cost.

articles.title: Holt Lunsford Commercial Investments acquires 26.5-acre site in North Fort Worth for industrial park development
articles.narrative: Holt Lunsford Commercial Investments (HLCI) has acquired a 26.5-acre site in North Fort Worth, TX, for the development of Meacham 820 Crossing, a two-building Class-A industrial park. The project will total approximately 238,000 square feet and is strategically located with direct frontage on I-820, offering efficient access to major transportation arteries and the Fort Worth Meacham International Airport. Construction is slated to begin in Q4 2026, with delivery anticipated in Q4 2027.

data_points.notable_features: Two Class A industrial buildings with 32-foot clear heights, dock-high loading, deep truck courts, and generous car parking, with accommodations for trailer parking and outside storage.
data_points.project_notes: Construction is expected to begin in Q4 2026.

articles.title: McShane Construction Company to build 93-unit affordable-housing community in Madison
articles.narrative: McShane Construction Company has been selected by Lincoln Avenue Communities to build Timberline Terrace, a 93-unit affordable housing community in Madison, Wisconsin. The podium-style building will feature five wood-framed stories over a below-grade precast garage and is designed to achieve Wisconsin Green Built Homes Gold Zero certification, incorporating sustainable features like a solar array and high-efficiency heat pumps. Completion is anticipated in fall 2027.

data_points.notable_features: Designed to achieve Wisconsin Green Built Homes Gold Zero certification, incorporating a solar array, high-efficiency heat pumps, and upgraded performance windows. Amenities include a 4,000-square-foot plaza with a playground and grill stations, a playroom, community room, lounge, community service space, and fitness area.

articles.title: Redline Property Partners acquires the 15 Building in downtown Minneapolis
articles.narrative: Redline Property Partners has acquired The 15 Building, a 12-story, 131,460-square-foot boutique office building in downtown Minneapolis. The property, now rebranded as "Studio 15," is adjacent to Redline's existing Andrus office building and features Art Deco design, recent renovations, and a strategic location with skyway connectivity and transit access. Redline plans to continue the building's amenitization program and invest in system improvements.

data_points.notable_features: Art Deco design elements, Bob Dylan mural, skyway connection, transit-oriented location, adjacent to Redline's Andrus office building.
data_points.project_notes: Building was previously renovated in 2018 with spec suites, bike room, and tenant lounge/conference center. Redline intends to continue amenitization and improve building systems.

articles.title: World Cup finals deliver last-minute windfall to NYC hotels
articles.narrative: New York City hotels experienced a last-minute surge in revenue due to the World Cup finals, with an additional $74 million generated on July 17-18 from an influx of visitors from Spain and Argentina. This unexpected boost, along with an anticipated $35 million to $40 million from the championship match, is expected to bring total incremental hotel revenue close to the initial $300 million projection for the tournament. However, this late windfall was not enough to offset an otherwise sluggish summer, as hotel occupancy has generally trailed last year's levels and the industry continues to face challenges from higher operating costs, weaker international tourism, and a slower post-pandemic recovery.

articles.title: Congressional committee eyes Compass partnership with Chicago MLS
articles.narrative: A Congressional subcommittee has requested a briefing from Compass CEO Robert Reffkin and Midwest Real Estate Data (MRED) CEO Rebecca Jensen regarding MRED's business practices and its partnership with Compass to implement its Private Listings Network. The subcommittee is investigating allegations of anticompetitive practices that could harm consumers by incentivizing brokers to push sellers towards private listings, potentially impacting housing affordability and creating conflicts of interest. This inquiry follows a federal antitrust lawsuit filed by Zillow against MRED and Compass, alleging a conspiracy to harm Zillow and force it to display Compass's private listings, which led to MRED cutting off Zillow's data feed in the Chicago area.

articles.title: Starwood files data center plan as Virginia residents revolt
articles.narrative: Starwood Capital Group has filed a permit application for a two-building data center project, Plaza 500, on a 34-acre site near the Alexandria town line in Virginia. The first building, Plaza 500 South, is planned for over 226,000 square feet. The project, which includes a substation, faces significant opposition from local residents concerned about its proximity to homes. Starwood previously acquired the site four years ago for $165 million.

data_points.notable_features: Includes a substation on site, located within 100 feet of homes in the Bren Mar neighborhood.
data_points.project_notes: Site previously acquired for $165 million four years ago.

articles.title: Grubb Properties forms $1.9B apartment REIT after recapitalization
articles.narrative: Grubb Properties has formed Link Apartments REIT, consolidating several of its funds into a private, non-traded multifamily REIT valued at approximately $1.9 billion. The new entity comprises 45 properties and over 5,600 units, aiming for a larger balance sheet and increased financing capabilities. Concurrently, Grubb Properties secured $617 million in financing, including a $377 million construction loan for its 8 Carlisle project in Manhattan and a $240 million credit facility for both the new REIT and its existing Opportunity Zone REIT.

data_points.address: 8 Carlisle Street, New York City, NY
data_points.notable_features: The 64-story tower is designed by Handel Architects and is expected to be the eighth-tallest residential building in Lower Manhattan.
data_points.project_notes: The site for 8 Carlisle Street was previously known as 111 Washington Street and was acquired by Grubb Properties in 2021 for $89 million. Construction passed the halfway point in spring 2026, with topping out expected in summer 2026.

articles.financing: The $377 million construction loan for 8 Carlisle includes a $300 million senior loan and a $77 million mezzanine loan. Grubb Properties also secured a $240 million credit facility applicable to both Link Apartments REIT and Link Apartments Opportunity Zone REIT.

articles.title: Wall Street landlords flip to sellers after housing law passage
articles.narrative: Institutional investors are increasingly listing single-family homes for sale following the passage of the 21st Century Road to Housing Act, which restricts their ability to acquire existing single-family properties. For-sale listings from these landlords have more than doubled in the last six months, reaching over 9,400 homes with a combined asking price of $3.1 billion. This shift indicates a strategic pivot by institutional investors, who are now net sellers, potentially reallocating capital towards the built-to-rent sector, which remains a viable growth path under the new legislation.

articles.title: Nir Meir fails to reach plea deal, will head to trial for fraud
articles.narrative: Nir Meir, former executive at HFZ Capital, has not reached a plea deal in his alleged $86 million fraud case related to the XI condo project. Despite his attorney's efforts to secure an agreement, Meir has pleaded not guilty and is set to proceed to trial in October. He is the only one of nine co-defendants who has not accepted a plea deal, with others receiving no jail time and minimal fines.

data_points.notable_features: Luxury condo project located on the High Line.
data_points.project_notes: Alleged $86 million fraud scheme involving diversion of funds from luxury real estate projects.

articles.title: JPMorgan eyes $425M valuation in exit from Fisher Brothers’ Third Avenue office tower
articles.narrative: JPMorgan Asset Management is seeking to sell its 49% stake in the 43-story, 1 million-square-foot office tower at 605 Third Avenue in New York City, with Fisher Brothers planning to bring in a new partner and recapitalize the asset. The transaction is targeting a valuation of $425 million, with the new investor partnering with Fisher Brothers to reposition the property and elevate it within the Grand Central competitive set. The building is currently 84% leased, and the business plan anticipates a 60% increase in income over the next five years by re-marking expiring leases.

data_points.address: 605 Third Avenue, New York City, NY
data_points.notable_features: 43-story office tower.
data_points.project_notes: JPMorgan Asset Management previously attempted to sell its stake in October 2020, seeking a $600 million valuation when the building was 97% leased.

articles.market_intelligence: Prime office areas like Park Avenue and Madison Avenue have vacancy rates of 6.5% and 11.5% respectively, while Third Avenue has a vacancy rate of 20.3%.

articles.title: Landlords sue Rent Guidelines Board over rent freeze decision
articles.narrative: A group of six landlords has filed a lawsuit against the New York Rent Guidelines Board, seeking to overturn its recent decision to freeze rents on stabilized apartments. The landlords allege that the board's process was a "sham" with a predetermined outcome, failing to adequately consider the economic conditions faced by property owners. This legal challenge, an Article 78 petition, is the first against the rent freeze and could potentially alter how rent increases are determined for rent-stabilized units in New York City.

articles.title: Mamdani turns to familiar figure to lead EDC
articles.narrative: Zohran Mamdani has appointed Anthony Shorris as the new president and CEO of the New York City Economic Development Corporation (EDC), filling a seven-month vacancy. Shorris, a veteran of New York City government with experience across multiple administrations and sectors, will lead the critical agency responsible for managing over 60 million square feet of real estate and overseeing more than 100 active development projects totaling $6 billion in construction investment. The EDC plays a significant role in city land development, business incentives, and other strategic initiatives, including piloting city-owned grocery stores.

articles.title: Historic cottage near Citadel’s Brickell HQ to move to Coconut Grove
articles.narrative: Ken Griffin is set to acquire the historic Dr. Jackson Medical Office cottage in Brickell for $2.98 million, pending City of Miami commission approval. The 121-year-old property, currently leased by Dade Heritage Trust, will be relocated to Coconut Grove, with Griffin funding its preservation and move. This transaction is part of Griffin's broader development plans for his Citadel headquarters site in Brickell, where the cottage occupies a key parcel.

data_points.notable_features: Historic wood-frame cottage, former office and surgical center of Miami's first resident physician.
data_points.project_notes: The property was originally located on Flagler Street in downtown Miami and moved to the Brickell Bay Drive area in 1917. The buyer previously arranged to move the William Jennings Bryan bayfront home from his Brickell Avenue estate to Vizcaya Museum & Gardens.

articles.title: Summermaxxing: Wealth boom brings heat to South Florida with pricey off-season sales
articles.narrative: South Florida's luxury and ultra-luxury residential markets are experiencing a robust off-season, with significant sales activity driven by a continuous influx of wealthy buyers. Brokers report a busier year than last, with single-family home and condo sales, particularly in the $1 million-plus range, showing substantial year-over-year increases across Miami-Dade, Broward, and Palm Beach counties. This trend is fueled by affluent transplants and a growing practice of "landmaxxing," where buyers acquire adjacent properties to expand their compounds, seeking greater space, privacy, and amenities. The surge in high-end demand has exacerbated the region's cost of living, pushing it past New York City and making South Florida the second most expensive area in the nation.

companies_people.firm_name: The Brokerage South Florida Real Estate

articles.title: Rivani’s $50M Miami Beach office expansion with Playboy HQ heads to voters
articles.narrative: Miami Beach voters will decide on a proposed $50 million rooftop expansion and a 106-year lease extension for The Rivani office building, which is slated to house Playboy's headquarters. The plan involves adding 47,000 square feet of office space, three padel courts, and a members club restaurant, while removing 250 parking spaces. In exchange for the extended ground lease, the investor is offering the city an annual rent increase of at least $500,000 and $1.5 million in public benefits, including funds for Lincoln Road improvements and infrastructure. The building, which was struggling with occupancy and rents when acquired in 2024, is now nearly fully leased and commands significantly higher rents, with a strong tenant mix.

data_points.notable_features: Proposed expansion includes office space, three rooftop padel courts, and a members club restaurant.
data_points.project_notes: The ground lease, approved in 1999, runs through 2052 with two 20-year renewal options. The proposed amendment would grant two additional 20-year renewal options, extending the lease through 2132. The investor previously acquired the building and ground lease for $62.5 million in 2024 and invested approximately $40 million in renovations. The city's annual base rent increase would start in 2033, and its share of gross revenue would rise from 2.5 percent to 3 percent. The investor must obtain a master building permit by July 1, 2031, and begin construction by Jan. 1, 2034, or the lease extension becomes void.

articles.title: Alonzo Mourning, HTG net $55M financing package for affordable housing
articles.narrative: Alonzo Mourning's AM Affordable Housing and Housing Trust Group secured a $55.4 million financing package for Artisan Pointe, a 115-unit affordable housing complex under construction in Naranja, an unincorporated area of south Miami-Dade County. The financing includes low-income housing tax credit equity, a permanent loan arranged by Berkadia, and funds from the Naranja Lakes Community Redevelopment Agency, along with a construction loan from U.S. Bancorp. This project is the first phase of a larger master-planned affordable development and is expected to be completed in January 2028, addressing the high demand for affordable housing in South Florida.

data_points.notable_features: Restricted to households earning at or less than 30 percent, 60 percent, and 70 percent of the area median income.
data_points.project_notes: The 4.3-acre site was previously acquired for $10.4 million in March 2026. This is the first phase of a master-planned affordable development, with a second phase planned for 160 units.

articles.market_intelligence: South Florida's median asking rent was $2,277 last month. Miami-Dade's area median income is $89,800. Market-rate multifamily developers are slowing construction due to oversupply, while affordable and workforce housing developers continue to build due to high demand and a housing crisis.

articles.title: $16M West Palm mansion breaks city’s record for priciest non-waterfront sale
articles.narrative: A newly constructed luxury mansion in West Palm Beach has sold for $15.7 million, setting a new record for the city's most expensive non-waterfront single-family home transaction. The sale of the 8,600-square-foot property reflects a growing trend of buyers seeking more spacious and relatively affordable luxury inland properties, especially as coastal prices and insurance premiums continue to rise. The transaction highlights the increasing demand for high-end homes away from the immediate waterfront, with prices per square foot in coastal West Palm Beach still considered a relative bargain compared to Palm Beach island.

data_points.address: 122 Blooomfield Drive, West Palm Beach, FL
data_points.notable_features: The home features five bedrooms, seven bathrooms, an elevator, private office, wine storage, and a 40-foot covered loggia with a summer kitchen, fireplace, pool, spa, and outdoor shower.
data_points.project_notes: The 2.9-acre lot was previously acquired for $2.9 million in 2024.

articles.market_intelligence: Coastal West Palm Beach homes are trading for $1,500 to $2,000 per square foot, while non-waterfront properties on Palm Beach island regularly trade for $3,000 to $4,000 per square foot. Inland luxury properties set a record last year with 123 transactions totaling $2.12 billion, a 65 percent increase in value and 41 percent increase in volume.

articles.title: Jiazhao “Frankie” Chen roped into another foreclosure suit as Chicago loan defaults near $100M
articles.narrative: A subsidiary of CoreVest Finance has filed a foreclosure lawsuit against Jiazhao "Frank" Chen and his entity Best Credit Investment LLC, seeking to recover nearly $820,000 on a defaulted loan. The lawsuit targets three multi-residential properties in Chicago's Bridgeport neighborhood, which are reportedly under construction and vacant. This action adds to Chen's growing legal challenges, with his total alleged real estate loan defaults in Chicago now approaching $100 million across a portfolio of over 55 properties.

data_points.address: 2628, 2634 and 2636 South Wells Street, Chicago, IL
data_points.notable_features: Multi-residential buildings, currently under construction and vacant.
data_points.project_notes: The lawsuit is over a defaulted loan payment of nearly $820,000 against Best Credit Investment LLC, for which Chen is the registered agent and individual guarantor. The original authorized debt under the revolving credit contract was $8.5 million.

articles.title: Habitat lists One333 apartment high-rise near The 78 amid rent surge
articles.narrative: Habitat is marketing its 305-unit One333 apartment high-rise in Chicago's South Loop for sale, nine years after acquiring it for $125 million. The property is being positioned to capitalize on its proximity to The 78 megadevelopment, which will include a new MLS stadium, and a projected surge in rents due to a slowdown in the area's multifamily construction pipeline. The building is 96% occupied with average rents of $2,799 per month, and its sale reflects a broader trend of downtown landlords cashing out amid rising prices.

data_points.notable_features: 28-story high-rise with two-story penthouses featuring European style kitchens, 20-foot ceilings, and private entrances. Amenities include a fitness center, social lounges, bike storage, and a pet spa. Located near The 78 megadevelopment, which will include a Major League Soccer stadium.
data_points.project_notes: Habitat acquired the building in 2017 for $125 million. The building was developed by CMK Companies.

articles.title: New Optima condo sales in Wilmette angling for North Shore sales records
articles.narrative: Optima Real Estate is launching sales for Optima Lumina, a 133-unit luxury condominium building in Wilmette, with prices for some units reaching $4.6 million, potentially setting a new sales record for the North Shore. The developer designed the units to be modular, allowing for combinations up to 5,000 square feet to meet buyer demand. Construction is expected to begin later this year, with initial occupancy projected for summer 2028.

data_points.notable_features: Luxury amenities include rooftop cold plunges, cooking stations, an indoor pool, and courtyard spaces. Units are designed to be modular, allowing for combinations up to 5,000 square feet.
data_points.project_notes: Optima Lumina is phase two of the Optima condo project in Wilmette. One-bedroom units start at $595,000, and three-bedroom units start just under $2 million.

articles.title: mHub eyes more than $1B industrial expansion in Kinzie Corridor
articles.narrative: The nonprofit advanced manufacturing incubator mHub is planning a significant industrial expansion in Chicago's Kinzie Corridor, aiming to develop a 72-acre industrial ecosystem called M+. The project, which could exceed $1 billion in total investment, will create a campus for startups, manufacturers, and researchers. The first phase is estimated at $250 million, with mHub seeking approximately $50 million in public funding from the city to support its development.

data_points.notable_features: Planned as an advanced manufacturing ecosystem combining modern industrial space with clean energy infrastructure.
data_points.project_notes: mHub is in talks to acquire a city block south of its facility at 240 North Ashland Avenue and 1640 West Walnut Street. The nonprofit previously received $17.6 million in TIF money for its 240 North Ashland Avenue purchase and redevelopment.

articles.title: Endeavor boosts Austin office pipeline with 5th and Walsh project
articles.narrative: Endeavor is moving forward with its 5th and Walsh project in Downtown Austin, a five-story, 198,000-square-foot office and retail building that will also serve as the developer's new headquarters. The project, which includes 21,000 square feet of ground-floor retail and a subterranean parking garage, is slated for completion in late 2028. Despite construction not yet commencing, nearly half of the office space is already pre-leased, indicating strong market demand.

data_points.notable_features: Includes 21,000 square feet of ground-floor restaurant and retail space and a below-grade parking garage.
data_points.project_notes: Plans for the project were initially submitted in March 2022. Endeavor will relocate its headquarters from 500 West 5th Street to this new building upon completion.

articles.title: Aerospace manufacturer moves HQ to Buda’s defense hub
articles.narrative: Even Platforms Incorporated, an aerospace manufacturer, is relocating its headquarters from the Dallas metro to Buda, Texas, after receiving a $50,000 incentive from the Buda City Council. The company will occupy a 9,000-square-foot facility within Tower Business Park, joining other defense companies in what is becoming a regional hub for the aerospace and defense industry. The incentive will support electrical service upgrades at the new facility, which Even Platforms plans to open for high school tours and internships to help revitalize the machine shop industry.

data_points.notable_features: Located in an industrial park that is a growing hub for aerospace and defense companies.
data_points.project_notes: Buda City Council approved a $50,000 incentive for electrical service upgrades at the facility.

articles.title: Jerry Jones-backed Legends Global named owner’s rep for new Dallas Mavericks arena
Clarion Partners offloads Sunnyvale offices to SFF Realty for $46M
articles.narrative: Clarion Partners, through an affiliate, has sold a 104,000-square-foot research and development office building in Sunnyvale, CA, to an affiliate of SFF Realty Partners for $46 million. The property is fully leased to a German tech company, which uses it as an engineering hub. The transaction highlights the continued investor interest in Silicon Valley's office and R&D market, driven by the presence of tech and artificial intelligence tenants.

data_points.notable_features: The building serves as an engineering hub focused on electrification and automated driving, with West Coast customer support also housed on-site.
data_points.project_notes: The tenant signed a 10-year lease in 2017.

articles.market_intelligence: Office vacancy in Silicon Valley fell to 14.4% in Q1. In Q2, Silicon Valley recorded its third consecutive quarter of net occupancy gains, totaling 313,357 square feet, a 123% year-over-year increase.

articles.title: Ashkenazy defaults on $40M loan tied to Union Square retail
articles.narrative: Ashkenazy Acquisitions is facing potential foreclosure on two Union Square retail properties in San Francisco due to a default on a $40 million loan. The properties, 1 Grant Avenue and 156 Geary Street, are struggling with vacancies and upcoming tenant departures, exacerbating the challenges of expensive debt in a recovering but still difficult retail market. The firm has 90 days to repay the outstanding debt of $41.1 million, though a loan modification or other resolution is still possible.

data_points.project_notes: The loan originated as $30 million in 2013 and was modified to $40 million in 2015. Ashkenazy acquired 1 Grant Avenue in 2015 for $16.3 million and 156 Geary Street in 2015 for $22.7 million. The firm previously put 1 Grant Avenue on the market in 2021, but a sale did not materialize.

articles.market_intelligence: Union Square has faced challenges with major retail departures post-pandemic, but is showing signs of recovery with new experiential concepts and recent investment, including a $48.5 million deal at 180 Post Street.

articles.title: Yellowstone seizes Parkmerced redevelopment sites through foreclosure
articles.narrative: Yellowstone Real Estate Investments has seized four parcels within the Parkmerced mega-development in San Francisco through foreclosure, stemming from a defaulted $101 million construction loan originated in 2022 for Maximus Real Estate. The debt had escalated to over $199 million with interest and fees, leading Yellowstone to acquire the properties via credit bids. These sites are entitled for nearly 1,700 residential units and represent the initial phases of a long-delayed redevelopment plan for the 152-acre community.

data_points.notable_features: The sites are entitled for nearly 1,700 residential units and are located next to San Francisco State University.
data_points.project_notes: The foreclosure stems from a construction loan originated in 2022. The redevelopment plan, approved in 2011, aimed to triple housing stock to over 5,600 units with new retail and transit stops, but never broke ground.

articles.title: Who was Clint Reilly?
articles.narrative: This article is an obituary for Clint Reilly, a prominent figure in San Francisco real estate, politics, and media, who passed away on July 19. Reilly was known for his long-term holding strategy in commercial real estate, amassing a portfolio valued at $400 million. His notable acquisitions included the Merchants Exchange Building, which he purchased in 1995 and recently refinanced, and the 235 Pine Street tower. Despite his reputation as a holder, Reilly recently sold several key assets, including the Little Fox Theater and 360 Pine Street, with the future of his remaining portfolio now uncertain.

articles.title: Billionaire Bill Koch finds buyer for Aspen compound at 75% off list price
articles.narrative: Billionaire industrialist Bill Koch has found a buyer for his 52-acre Aspen compound, Elk Mountain Lodge, which sold for over $33.5 million through an auction. The sale price represents a significant discount from its previous asking price of $125 million. Koch, who acquired the property in 2007 for $26.5 million and expanded it, had been attempting to sell the estate for over a decade.

data_points.notable_features: The compound includes an eight-bedroom main lodge and seven other cabins, one of which is a 3,100-square-foot gym. The main house features two offices, two hot tubs, and temperature-controlled wine storage.
data_points.project_notes: The property was originally purchased in 2007 for $26.5 million and converted from an event venue to a private residence. A 31-acre parcel was added to the property, then sold in 2020 for $14.5 million. The estate was rented out in 2023 and 2024 for an asking rent of $300,000 per week.

articles.market_intelligence: Aspen's real estate market has experienced a post-Covid downturn, with a 44% decline in sales during the first half of the year compared to the same period last year. Transactions exceeding $10 million saw an even steeper drop, falling 48% year-over-year.

articles.title: Walker Webcast: Willy Walker Cuts Through the Market Noise
articles.narrative: Willy Walker, Chairman and CEO of Walker & Dunlop, addressed the commercial real estate market's slow recovery, noting that the anticipated rebound in 2025 did not materialize, leading to a new industry mantra of "slice of heaven in '27." He emphasized the importance of analyzing data to cut through market noise, highlighting the steady employment rate despite AI fears. Walker also pointed out the growing disparity in AI token usage between China and the U.S., raising national security concerns. He discussed the disconnect between low consumer sentiment and a strong stock market, suggesting political divisiveness or ongoing conflicts as potential causes. Finally, Walker warned of a significant wave of CRE loan maturities expected between 2029 and 2031 due to a recent trend of shorter loan durations.

articles.narrative: The historic Cinerama Dome and an adjacent 14-screen movie complex in Hollywood, which have been closed since the pandemic, are slated to reopen in 2028 under the management of Alamo Drafthouse Cinema, a subsidiary of Sony Pictures Entertainment. The Cinerama Dome, a cultural landmark since 1963, will undergo restorative renovations to preserve its unique moviegoing experience and iconic branding. This lease agreement is seen as a significant endorsement for the future of theatrical entertainment and the enduring appeal of shared cinematic experiences.

articles.title: Jon Pezzoni Joins Hunneman’s Leasing & Advisory Team as SVP
articles.narrative: Jon Pezzoni has joined Hunneman's Leasing & Advisory team as Senior Vice President and Principal, bringing over a decade of experience in the Greater Boston office, R&D, and industrial markets. Pezzoni, previously an SVP at Avison Young, specializes in advising tenants, landlords, and developers in the Metro West, 495 West & South submarkets, focusing on strategies to maximize asset value. His expertise and local relationships are expected to enhance Hunneman's client services.

articles.title: Proposed EB-5 Rule Clamping Down On Bridge Financing Rattles Sector
articles.narrative: The U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) has released a draft rulebook for the EB-5 program, introducing significant changes that could impact real estate development financing. A key proposal restricts the use of bridge financing, a popular method for EB-5 investors to qualify for visas, by imposing stricter job creation standards. This shift aims to enhance program integrity but has raised concerns among industry stakeholders that it could disqualify many projects currently in the pipeline and reduce investment flow. The industry is preparing to submit public comments, hoping USCIS will adjust the rules to prevent disruption.

articles.title: What Charlotte Wants To Learn During Its 150-Day Moratorium On New Data Centers
articles.narrative: Charlotte has implemented a 150-day moratorium on new data center development, which began in June, to address growing concerns over the environmental impact and resource demands of these facilities. City officials are researching best practices from other jurisdictions and engaging with stakeholders to formulate new policies, with a potential extension of the pause. This move follows heated debate, particularly concerning a proposed project by American Tower Corp. near a nature preserve, and reflects a broader national trend of local governments re-evaluating data center growth due to significant water and power consumption.

data_points.project_notes: Charlotte approved a 150-day moratorium on new data center development in June, with a potential extension. The proposed American Tower Corp. project's rezoning request has been delayed until at least November.

articles.market_intelligence: More than 100 local governments across the U.S. are grappling with data center development issues. Davie County, NC, passed a one-year data center moratorium. New York became the first state to impose a yearlong ban on data center construction.

articles.title: REPORT: Google Quadruples Miami Office After Founders' Mansion Buys

This expansion follows recent high-profile residential real estate purchases in the area by the company's founders. The move reflects a broader trend of out-of-state companies increasing their presence in South Florida, often after their leadership relocates to the region.

articles.title: Startup Building AI Agents For Landlords Raises $12M
articles.narrative: Uniti, a proptech startup specializing in AI agents for landlord operations and leasing, has successfully closed a $12 million Series A funding round. The New York-based company's AI agents automate various tasks, including scheduling tours, managing inquiries, handling collections, and processing payments for landlords. This funding will enable Uniti to expand its business and accelerate growth across multiple verticals, particularly in operationally intensive asset classes like self-storage, senior living, and manufactured housing.

articles.title: Bank OZK Continues To Cut Real Estate Portfolio
articles.narrative: Bank OZK is continuing to reduce its exposure to real estate, with its real estate loan book falling to 47% of its total portfolio in Q2 2026, down from 52% in Q1. This strategic shift, aimed at cutting nonperforming assets, resulted in the slowest second quarter for real estate loan originations in five years, totaling $1 billion. The bank is facing headwinds from sponsors struggling to raise equity for new construction due to macro uncertainty and high material prices, though data center projects are a notable exception in the broader construction pipeline. Bank OZK anticipates its real estate exposure will eventually align with its corporate and institutional banking segment, which currently represents 22.2% of its loan portfolio, a target it hopes to achieve next year.
articles.market_intelligence: The country's overall construction pipeline is improving, primarily driven by data center projects. A surge in debt liquidity and significant competition for deals that secure equity have also been observed in the market.
